title: One crown, one law?
hook: Did the two British texts set one rule for property disputes and criminal cases?

knows: A legal rule can apply to a named kind of dispute.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish prescribed court standards from domain-specific 1774 legal provisions, without claiming uniform practice or Indigenous-law erasure.

misconception: Yes; both use one undifferentiated prescription

claims.text: These are British colonial prescriptions, not observed practice, Indigenous law, consent or title. Religious-order, common-soccage and wills exceptions apply; provisions permit alteration. Former instruments’ revocation after 1 May 1775 differs from the Act’s label. Contemporary Kahnawà:ke and joint Huron-Wendat/Canada records represent distinct, not universal perspectives. Paris Article IV separately cedes Canada and dependencies from the French Crown to the British Crown. Avalon’s English transcription is not collation of the French original. Interstate cession differs from those legal prescriptions and establishes neither Indigenous title nor consent.
